clusters.label: Hidden native default and its override
clusters.family: Verify undocumented behaviour of the rendered element
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know what the component hard-codes on its underlying native element by default (in this data, the button `type`) and whether a caller can override it, because that fact decides a downstream behaviour such as implicit form submission. The props table is silent on it, and a test-style story's name literally asserts the default, so that story is the one documented place the fact is stated.
clusters.include: Loads of a story named for a default value on the rendered element, to confirm the default and/or whether it can be changed. Includes re-loads of an already-printed story to isolate that one fact, and loads made to corroborate what the bundle or typings had already shown.
clusters.exclude: General 'are refs/native props forwarded' or 'what native element is rendered' questions answered by a story named for that capability go to k02. The same type/submit question asked of a story NOT named for it (Anatomy, Variants, the last unread story) goes to k03. Looking for submit wiring in an app-context example goes to k07. Rule: k01 only when the need is the default value (and its override) and the story name states that default.

clusters.label: Native element exposure named by story
clusters.family: Verify undocumented behaviour of the rendered element
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know whether a ref and arbitrary native attributes reach the underlying element, or what native element is rendered at all, which the short props table does not list. A story whose name states that capability (forwards ref and props, native control, a native attribute) is taken as direct evidence.
clusters.include: Ref and prop forwarding checks (e.g. to move focus to an element), general pass-through questions, and 'is it a native control and how is it driven' questions, when the story name speaks to the capability directly.
clusters.exclude: Questions about one specific default value and whether it can be overridden go to k01. The same pass-through question asked of a story not named for it goes to k03. className wanted as a styling hook goes to k13. Rule: if the need is phrased as general forwarding ('native attributes such as type') rather than 'does it default to X', it is k02 even when the story loaded is the default-type one.

clusters.label: Probing other stories for native-attribute support
clusters.family: Verify undocumented behaviour of the rendered element
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know whether a component accepts or forwards native attributes (type, name, autocomplete) or can act as a submit control, but no story addresses that directly. It loads a structural, catalogue, adjacent-prop or last-unread story hoping its source incidentally reveals the rendered element or a pass-through.
clusters.include: Anatomy, Variants, Class Name, or the only/last unseen story loaded to look for a type or submit option, the rendered element, or native-attribute pass-through; includes checking whether a behaviour already seen in the bundle is a documented pattern when the story is only indirectly related.
clusters.exclude: Story name states the fact: k01 or k02. App-context example checked for native field attributes: k08; for form or submit wiring: k07. Anatomy loaded for parts, slots or basic wiring with no native-attribute question: k11. Variants loaded to find visual looks: k10. Tie-break with k11: if the need names native attributes or the type of the rendered element as what the story should expose, it is k03 even if parts are also mentioned.

clusters.label: Edge behaviour at value limits
clusters.family: Verify undocumented behaviour of the rendered element
clusters.definition: The agent needs the runtime rule for what the component does at its boundaries (disable versus clamp at min/max, whether a value can reach zero), which the default values in the props table do not spell out. A story named for the bounds behaviour, rather than for a single prop, promises exactly that rule.
clusters.include: Loads of a limits/bounds behaviour story to learn what happens at the extremes and whether that behaviour suits the intended use.
clusters.exclude: How min/max are set as one detail of copying an in-context example goes to k05. What range is reported to assistive technology goes to k15. An item stays here even when the previous story was an opaque wrapper, as long as the story now loaded is a different one chosen for its bounds behaviour.

clusters.label: In-context composition template to copy
clusters.family: Model on the design system's in-context example
clusters.definition: The agent is about to build or rewrite a concrete piece of app UI and wants the design system's own rendition of that same (or a closely analogous) UI as a template: how the component sits among its neighbours, which props each instance gets, how rows, sections or container contents are arranged. The story's name or description matches the target screen, unlike the single-prop demos beside it.
clusters.include: App-context examples (a list row with an embedded control, a full form, a side panel, a complete dialog) loaded for layout, per-instance props, bounds, labelling, grouping and ancillary controls. Includes multi-aspect 'how is the reference form structured' needs that enumerate grouping, headings and per-field props rather than only wrapper and submit.
clusters.exclude: Need narrowed to primary-versus-secondary emphasis: k06. Narrowed to form wrapper and submission only: k07. Lead question is native field attributes: k08. About how status or progress is conveyed: k09. Lead question is whether or which control the reference uses: k17. Need is what a hidden helper renders: k18. Rule: the control is already chosen and the need is how to arrange and configure it in the target UI.

clusters.label: In-context primary versus secondary actions
clusters.family: Model on the design system's in-context example
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know how the design system places a primary action together with a secondary one and which props give one more visual weight, when the component has no explicit variant prop. An app-context story depicting exactly that action group is the model for both arrangement and prop combination.
clusters.include: Loads of the app-context action-group example to learn stacked versus side-by-side layout and the props distinguishing the two actions, including an after-the-fact check of an already built layout against the reference.
clusters.exclude: The same example loaded to look for submit or form wiring goes to k07. A variants catalogue loaded to enumerate available looks goes to k10. Rule: if the item mentions both, decide by whether the need asks about emphasis/layout (k06) or submission (k07).

clusters.label: Reference form wrapper and submit wiring
clusters.family: Model on the design system's in-context example
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know whether the design system's own app-context example uses a native form element and how submission is triggered (submit-type button, form wrapper, submit handler), since the component docs document neither. An app-context story named for the screen or flow being fixed is the likeliest place a sanctioned pattern would appear.
clusters.include: Whole-form or action-button examples from the target flow loaded to see a form wrapper, a submit control or a handler to copy, whichever component's story it is.
clusters.exclude: The default button type read from a story named for it: k01. Reference form loaded for its overall structure (sections, headings, per-field props, error messages listed alongside the form element): k05. Lead question is which native attributes the fields receive: k08. Hunting for a submit option in Anatomy/Variants: k03.

clusters.label: Native field attributes in reference example
clusters.family: Model on the design system's in-context example
clusters.definition: The agent wants to see whether the design system's own app-context example passes native attributes (name, type, autocomplete) that the props table omits, treating real usage as evidence that they are supported and intended. The app-context story is chosen because it is the design system's version of the very form under repair.
clusters.include: Reference form example loaded with the lead question 'which native attributes do its fields receive', even if grouping is mentioned second.
clusters.exclude: Same question asked of an Anatomy or sole story: k03. Whether the example has a form wrapper and how it submits: k07. Multi-aspect structure where attributes are only one item in a list led by form element and grouping: k05.

clusters.label: How the reference conveys current status
clusters.family: Model on the design system's in-context example
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know how the design system's in-context example makes a state or progress change perceivable: which values and label the component receives, what visible text accompanies it, and how it is named for assistive technology. A story modelling the app's own indicator is the vehicle because it shows the component together with its surrounding text.
clusters.include: In-context indicator examples loaded for value/max/label choices, step wording, accompanying heading or copy, and accessible labelling; includes re-fetches of that example when the stated need is still how status is conveyed.
clusters.exclude: Test or anatomy stories about what ARIA the component exposes on its own: k15. Prop-named stories about the naming prop: k14. Need is explicitly what markup sits behind a one-line wrapper: k18. Pure layout and wiring of a control in its row or container: k05.

clusters.label: Catalogue of available visual variants
clusters.family: Learn the component's vocabulary, parts and wiring
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know which looks or variants a component offers and which props select them, when the props table shows only a few flags or no variant prop. A story named as the catalogue (Variants), or a basic overview story expected to enumerate options, is the natural place to see all styles side by side.
clusters.include: Loads aimed at enumerating styles to find a secondary look, or a colour/variant option for distinguishing statuses, regardless of which story name was used.
clusters.exclude: In-context pairing of a primary and secondary action: k06. className wanted to create a look that does not exist: k13. A variants catalogue scanned for a non-visual capability such as a submit option: k03.

clusters.label: Parts, slots and basic wiring
clusters.family: Learn the component's vocabulary, parts and wiring
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know what a component consists of and how to write a basic working usage: its parts or slots, value/onChange or open/close props, where a label goes. The docs gave only a props table or an opaque example, so a structural overview story (Anatomy, or the component's one story) is expected to show the whole component.
clusters.include: Structural story loaded to learn composition and wiring before using the component, including after an in-context example turned out to be an opaque wrapper, and for containers what goes inside and how it is arranged.
clusters.exclude: Structural story loaded to decide between controls or find when-to-use guidance: k16. To find native-attribute or type support: k03. To learn ARIA exposure (cue is about ARIA/announcement): k15. Unlisted, guessed story name for state wiring: k12. Rule versus k15: decide by what the cue says the story was expected to deliver, parts (k11) or assistive-technology behaviour (k15).

clusters.label: Guessed story for open-state wiring
clusters.family: Learn the component's vocabulary, parts and wiring
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know how a stateful overlay is driven (open prop, close callback, content while open), and no listed story showed it. It requests a conventional story name it guessed (e.g. 'Open') that never appeared in any listing.
clusters.include: Loads of a story whose name was guessed from convention rather than read from a listing, in order to see controlled-state wiring.
clusters.exclude: The same question asked of a listed structural story goes to k11. Rule: k12 only when the cue says the story name was guessed/unlisted.

clusters.label: className as styling escape hatch
clusters.family: Learn the component's vocabulary, parts and wiring
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know whether a component accepts className (and extra attributes) so the app can produce a look or placement the component does not offer out of the box. The story named for the className prop is the documented evidence of that hook.
clusters.include: Class Name stories loaded to check whether custom colours, styling or positioning can be applied from outside.
clusters.exclude: Class Name story used as indirect evidence that native attributes pass through: k03. Which built-in variants exist: k10.

clusters.label: Accessible name mechanism and wording
clusters.definition: The agent needs to know how a control gets its accessible name and what that name should say: the phrasing, what it names, whether a label prop is visible or assistive-only. A story named after the naming prop or rule (aria-label, label, icon-only needs a label) promises a worked example of the intended name.
clusters.include: Prop-named or rule-named stories loaded for the wording and passing of an accessible name, including what a label prop actually does.
clusters.exclude: What roles, values or announcements the component exposes by itself: k15. Labelling as one detail of an in-context example: k05 or k09.

clusters.label: Semantics exposed to assistive technology
clusters.definition: The agent needs the component's built-in assistive-technology behaviour: how an error is announced, whether the error node is always in the DOM, what role, range or values are reported. A test-style or anatomy story whose name or description states that accessibility behaviour is the documented evidence.
clusters.include: Loads of stories named for announcement, always-mounted slots or range reporting, and of structural stories whose description is about ARIA, to learn what is exposed without extra work by the caller.
clusters.exclude: Wording or mechanism of the accessible name: k14. How an in-context example conveys status with surrounding text: k09. Anatomy loaded for parts with accessibility wiring as a secondary question: k11.

clusters.label: Generic story mined for usage guidance
clusters.family: Decide which component fits the job
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know what a component is for and when to use it rather than a sibling control, and found no written guidance. It loads the component's only story or its Anatomy hoping the description or structure reveals intended use.
clusters.include: Sole-story or Anatomy loads where the need or trigger frames the look as resolving which control fits (compare with another control, 'when to use', 'intended use'), typically after docs, guideline searches or an in-context example yielded nothing.
clusters.exclude: An app-context example used as precedent for which control the design system uses: k17. Structural story loaded simply to learn how to write the component: k11. Rule: mention of a rival control or of missing which-control guidance in need or trigger puts it here.

clusters.label: Which control the reference uses
clusters.family: Decide which component fits the job
clusters.definition: The agent wants to know which component the design system itself uses for a given job in the app's own context, to resolve an inconsistency or a choice between controls. An app-context story is loaded as precedent, either for the candidate control or for the rival control to see what it is really meant for.
clusters.include: In-context examples loaded with the lead question 'is X the intended control here' or 'what does the design system use Y for in this app'.
clusters.exclude: Control already chosen and the example loaded for layout, props and wiring: k05. Generic story mined for guidance: k16. Rule: decide by the lead question of the need; 'is it / which control' leads here, 'how is it laid out with X' leads to k05.

clusters.label: Seeing behind an opaque helper
clusters.family: Recover source hidden behind a helper
clusters.definition: The story's source as already displayed was a one-line wrapper or helper that hid the real markup or call the agent needed. The agent loads that same story individually hoping for fuller source than the docs page gave.
clusters.include: Needs that explicitly ask what a hidden helper or wrapper renders, or what markup sits behind an example whose source had already been printed.
clusters.exclude: After an opaque example, moving on to a different story goes to that story's cluster (k11, k16, k04). Re-loading an already-printed story to confirm a named fact stays with the fact (k01). A re-fetch whose stated need is still the substantive question, with no reference to hidden markup, stays in that question's cluster (e.g. k09).
